limitations.statement: No last-iterate or almost-sure epsilon-stationarity guarantee; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim. A minimum-gradient iterate exists but selecting it is not implemented by this oracle.

performance_links.scope_note: Expected squared gradient for this explicit output adapter only; read all Theorem conditions and source issues.

variants.cost: N joint gradient-pair queries (or N calls to each partial-gradient oracle), N Euclidean projections, N vector updates per block, and one uniform-index selection. No inner maximization, function-value query or grad Phi evaluation. Projection arithmetic and storage are separately charged; retaining all x iterates uses O(Nm) storage, while reservoir sampling uses O(m+n) state.
variants.name: Two-time-scale GDA with proof-aligned random output
variants.output: Draw J uniformly in {0,...,N-1} independently of the deterministic trajectory; return x_J. This is a local output adapter; source Algorithm 1 instead draws from x1,...,xT.
public_inputs: ell>=mu>0, kappa=ell/mu>=1, projection onto Y, integer horizon N>=1; optionally epsilon>0 and valid upper bounds on Delta and diameter D
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,N-1 query (gx,gy)=(grad_x f(x_t,y_t),grad_y f(x_t,y_t)); set x_(t+1)=x_t-eta_x gx and y_(t+1)=P_Y(y_t+eta_y gy), both using the old pair.
variants.requirements: Exact gradients of f:R^(m+n)->R at one shared old iterate; Euclidean projection onto nonempty closed convex Y. For the linked performance: joint ell-smoothness, mu-strong concavity in y, diameter <=D, and finite Delta=Phi(x0)-inf Phi.
variants.state_and_initialization: x0 in R^m, y0 in Y; retain pre-update x iterates or use uniform reservoir sampling.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: eta_x=1/[16(kappa+1)^2 ell], eta_y=1/ell. Stop after N updates. With valid gap/diameter bounds, epsilon RMS stationarity follows for N>=max(1,ceil((256 Delta/(103 eta_x)+576 kappa ell^2 D^2/103)/epsilon^2)). Computing those bounds is not included in gradient cost.
